div.head: Hn Lond 14
div.ab: Quodsi reddere noluerint neque ad disrationandum uenire, tunc ciues, quibus debita sua debent, capiant in ciuitatem namia sua uel de burgo uel uilla uel de comitatu, in quo manet qui debitum debet.
Quodsi reddere noluerint neque ad disrationandum venire, tunc cives, quibus debita sua debent, capiant in civitatem namia sua vel de [burgo vel villa vel de] comitatu in quo manet qui debitum debet.

But if they have refused to pay or to come to clear themselves, then the citizens to whom they are in debt shall seize their pledges [and bring them] into the city from the [town, village or] county in which the debtor lives.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 292–293 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text added from Gesetze I p. 525, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

Dass hierüber placita apud Londonias stattfinden, sagt auch Freibrief 1155; dagegen die Exekutive bleibt dort fort. K. Johann gab dann die Klausel De debitis quod debitores in civitate si venerint uel sui [Angehörige] distringantur; vgl. Bateson EHR 1902, 726.—Stubbs nimmt die Einschiebung{45} ‘dass sie nicht schulden’ in den Text; Lect. 128; die Worte burgo uel uilla lässt er fort

That placita apud Londonias are held on this matter is also stated by the charter of 1155; the provision for enforcement, on the other hand, is omitted there. King John then granted the clause De debitis quod debitores in civitate si venerint uel sui [their kin] distringantur; cf. Bateson EHR 1902, 726.—Stubbs takes the interpolation{45} ‘that they do not owe’ into the text; Lect. 128; he omits the words burgo uel uilla

Pfändung de vicino debitoris begegnet in anderen städtischen Freibriefen (Ballard 164); die des in derselben Grafschaft (s. d. Gl 12. 21b) Heimischen in Repressalie auch zu Colchester 1189; communi dafür scheint mir aus comitatu nur verlesen, gegen Bateson Bor. cust. I 120. II p. liii

Distraint de vicino debitoris occurs in other town charters (Ballard 164); distraint, by way of reprisal, of a man resident in the same shire (see that word in Gl 12. 21b) also at Colchester 1189; communi there seems to me merely a misreading of comitatu, against Bateson Bor. cust. I 120. II p. liii
